title: Peptides on metal nanostructures
summary: Short peptides can stabilize and functionalize gold and silver nanostructures. We use molecular dynamics to study how peptide sequence controls adsorption, structural stability and hydrogen bonding at the metal surface, in collaboration with experimental groups that synthesize and test these materials.
alt: Render of a nanoparticle with a metallic core covered by a shell of molecules.

title: Hybrid nanoparticles and membranes
summary: Lipid and lipid-polymer nanoparticles are promising carriers for targeted therapy. We simulate how their composition and coating determine which membranes they recognize and how cells take them up, with current theses on predictive design of lipid coatings, uptake by macrophages and photocontrollable nanocarriers.
alt: Render of a coated nanoparticle embedded in a layer of molecules.

title: Functional surfaces for ion capture
summary: Peptides and other molecules anchored to nanosurfaces can capture ions selectively. Current theses explore cyclic peptides on nanosurfaces for the environmental remediation of ionic pollutants, and nanomaterials for the selective capture and release of ions in mining processes.
alt: Close-up render of peptide chains lying on a flat surface with small ions above them.

title: Membrane proteins and peptide biomaterials
summary: With experimental collaborators we study ion channels and their regulation by lipids and toxins, antimicrobial peptides at lipid membranes, and peptide-based materials such as collagen-like peptides and hydrogels for tissue repair.
